News article, representing the core reading journey and article metadata template.
Latest-news listing, representing chronological section/listing templates.
Sign-in modal, representing account input, validation, and recovery affordances.
Unknown URL, representing HTTP/navigation failure recovery.

findings.summary: The site remains light under the user’s dark preference.
findings.evidence: Dark-emulation screenshot is visually identical to the light surface; computed html color-scheme is normal and the page remains white beneath the modal.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and retint page, modal, navigation, text, and controls through prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Live indicators keep blinking when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, four live blink animations remain running at 3000 ms and no reduced-motion CSS rule was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce branch that stops nonessential blink and entry animations.

findings.summary: Consent and notification prompts obscure the primary content on first load.
findings.evidence: Load screenshots on homepage, listing, and article show a blocking consent modal covering the primary content.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-blocking consent entry point with equal choices and defer notification subscription until the user asks for it.

findings.summary: The blocking consent overlay is custom role-based chrome rather than a native dialog primitive.
findings.evidence: The visible consent surface is a DIV with role=dialog rather than a native dialog; no dialog or popover element was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog for the modal flow with native focus management and a clear, equivalent dismissal path.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated on the first primary link.
findings.evidence: Programmatically focused first visible link computed outline-style none and box-shadow none, so keyboard focus is not visibly indicated.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a high-contrast :focus-visible outline for every interactive element and verify the full tab sequence.

findings.summary: The cold-load experience is slow and script-heavy.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse performance was 0.48 with simulated LCP 6,014 ms and TBT 521 ms; CLS was excellent at 0.000056. HAR recorded 112 requests and 3,555,827 transferred bytes, including 2,940,302 script bytes; Lighthouse flagged render-blocking and font-display opportunities.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP asset, shorten render-blocking chains, split and defer noncritical/third-party scripts, and retest on mobile throttling.

findings.summary: Large amounts of JavaScript and CSS are shipped but unused during the homepage load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 1,096 KiB unused JavaScript and 127 KiB unused CSS across 18 resources.
findings.suggestedFix: Route-split feature and ad bundles, remove dead CSS, and load account/consent/vendor code only when its surface is needed.

findings.summary: Some controls have mismatched accessible names and visible labels, and some images lack alt attributes.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 9 visible-label/accessibility-name mismatches; the image probe also found 11 images lacking alt attributes. Lighthouse found 3 insufficient-contrast instances.
findings.suggestedFix: Align aria-label text with visible labels, add appropriate empty or descriptive alt values, and correct the three failing color pairs.

findings.summary: Image sizing and responsive delivery are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Document has HTML doctype and UTF-8, but Lighthouse found an incorrect image aspect ratio and low-resolution image; image probe found 4 missing dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct aspect ratios, reserve dimensions, and provide accurate responsive srcset/sizes for card and article images.

findings.summary: Large first-party scripts lack source maps and Chrome reports inspector issues.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found missing source maps for 3 large first-party scripts and Chrome Inspector issues, though deprecated API and BFCache checks passed.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish production source maps securely and resolve the recorded DevTools Issues panel diagnostics.

findings.summary: Browser security policy and cookie hardening are incomplete.
findings.evidence: HTTPS and HSTS are present, but CSP allows unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval; nosniff is missing and all 13 observed cookies were flagged insecure. Headers probe found no frame protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or X-Content-Type-Options; CSP lacks frame-ancestors and allows unsafe script modes.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unsafe script allowances with nonces/hashes, add nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy, and mark all cookies Secure with appropriate SameSite.

findings.summary: The anonymous homepage activates an unusually broad tracking and partner footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker probe found 43 third-party origins and 8 known tracker families; consent text states data may be shared with 231 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Default to data minimisation, gate nonessential vendors until affirmative consent, reduce partner count, batch analytics, and document each vendor’s value.

findings.summary: The login and consent/account handoff lacks humane validation and modern input assistance.
findings.evidence: Submitting the visible login with empty email/password produced no validation message, role=alert, aria-invalid state, or native invalidity. Visible email and password fields have labels but both autocomplete attributes are empty. The refusal CTA reads “RECHAZAR Y REGISTRARSE”.
findings.suggestedFix: Separate consent refusal from registration, add email/current-password autocomplete, required semantics, accessible post-interaction errors, and a passkey option.

findings.summary: Unknown URLs silently become the homepage instead of a useful not-found state.
findings.evidence: Unknown URL redirected to the normal homepage without identifying the failure or preserving the requested context.
findings.suggestedFix: Return HTTP 404 with a clear explanation, search, relevant sections, and a route back while preserving the requested URL.

findings.summary: Network, third-party, and legacy-image costs are disproportionate to the text-led page.
findings.evidence: Of 100 images, 88 use legacy formats, 79 lack srcset, 5 are oversized, and 5 below-fold images are not lazy-loaded. HAR transferred 3.56 MB and tracker evidence found 43 third-party origins, disproportionate for a text-led news homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a page-weight/vendor budget, defer nonessential third parties, use responsive AVIF/WebP, and lazy-load below-fold media.

findings.summary: The settled homepage has a very large heap and object population for a news listing.
findings.evidence: A settled homepage heap contained 961,911 nodes and 55,031,124 self-size bytes, including 58,508 closures, which is disproportionate for a news listing.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile retained vendor/component trees, remove unused closures/listeners, bound caches, and repeat baseline/target/final heap comparisons after script reduction.

taskList.title: Replace the coercive blocking consent/registration experience with equal, privacy-minimised choices
Reduce and defer script/vendor cost to restore fast LCP and a bounded footprint
Harden CSP, browser policies, and cookie flags
Restore visible focus and fix accessible names, contrast, and alt coverage
Modernise responsive image delivery and reserve correct dimensions
Add dark and reduced-motion preference styles
Fix source maps and remaining inspector diagnostics
